stem: A client has confirmed iron-deficiency anemia. Which red blood cell morphology should the nurse expect on the peripheral smear?

options.A: Predominantly macrocytic, deeply hemoglobinized red cells
options.B: Microcytic, hypochromic red cells with increased central pallor
options.C: Predominantly normal-sized red cells with no change in pallor
options.D: Large spherocytes with absent central pallor as the defining pattern

rationale: The 2026 StatPearls review of iron deficiency describes the peripheral smear in iron-deficiency anemia as microcytic and hypochromic, with an enlarged central zone of pallor and a thin hemoglobinized rim. Therefore B is the expected morphology. The other choices describe different or nonspecific red-cell patterns and do not match the source-defined iron-deficiency smear.
educational_objective: Recognize microcytic, hypochromic red cells with increased central pallor as the expected peripheral-smear morphology in iron-deficiency anemia.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine, NCBI Bookshelf — StatPearls
source_document_title: Iron Deficiency and Microcytic Hypochromic Anemia
source_locator: Histopathology and Figure 'Iron Deficiency Anemia': peripheral smear demonstrates microcytic, hypochromic red blood cells with enlarged central pallor and a thin hemoglobinized rim
source_claim_supported: Iron-deficiency anemia characteristically produces microcytic, hypochromic red blood cells with increased central pallor on peripheral smear.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Appendix A, Reduction of Risk Potential > Laboratory Values, printed p.43 / PDF p.47: compare client laboratory values to normal laboratory values and monitor client laboratory values
blueprint_topic: Reduction of Risk Potential — Laboratory Values / hematologic morphology
correction_summary: The source item attempted to diagnose iron deficiency from a microcytic-hypochromic smear alone, which is not unique because thalassemia and lead toxicity can also produce that pattern. Reversed the construct: the diagnosis is established and the learner identifies the expected morphology. Removed the B12 narrative, rebuilt parallel morphology distractors, and used the updated 2026 StatPearls exact locator.
audit_findings: B is directly supported by the current StatPearls histopathology section. The revised stem removes the original second-answer/etiologic ambiguity. A, C, and D are clearly distinct morphologic patterns and do not overlap with the source-defined iron-deficiency morphology. No unsupported ferritin threshold, diagnostic exclusivity claim, cueing, or unresolved conflict remains.
